A backyard made
for the whole family

One warm, natural-red paver patio with dining by the door, a lounge under the tree and a fire pit corner, so the yard gets used every day.

Where we’re starting

Your backyard today

Great bones: a beautiful shade tree, roses along the house and room to gather. What’s missing is one solid outdoor floor that ties it all together.

The plan

One patio, three places to be

Built on the layout we walked together: dining right outside the entrance, a lounge in the shade of the tree, and a fire pit corner on the narrow side.

Dining by the entrance
Step out of the house straight to the table. Meals, platters and drinks are only a few steps from the kitchen.
Lounge under the tree
The sofa and chairs face the tree, in its shade, on a level, clean surface.
Fire pit corner
The narrow side becomes a cozy fire pit spot for evenings with the family.
The tree & roses stay
A planting ring keeps the tree healthy, and the roses keep their bed along the house.

Drawn up from the sketch Roy made on your visit.

The look

Natural, warm, reddish

A blend of rust, clay, tan and soft brown that looks like natural stone. It’s warm next to the cream house and the green garden, and it never looks flat or new-construction.

Why pavers

Made for family life

They don’t crack

Pavers flex with the ground. If one ever gets stained or damaged, we swap that single piece.

Safe underfoot

A textured, non-slip surface for kids, grandparents and bare feet.

Low maintenance

No mowing and no mud. Locked joint sand keeps weeds and ants out.

Use it all year

Dry and level after rain, so it’s ready for dinners, birthdays and holidays.

The extra mile

Built to stay flat for decades

Most patio problems start where nobody looks: under the pavers. That’s where we put in the extra time, because it’s the difference between a patio that looks great for a year and one that still looks great in twenty.

Layout & protection

Mark the plan on site, locate utilities, and protect the house, AC unit, tree and roses before any digging starts.

Dig out to firm ground

Lawn, roots, soft soil and the old brick all come out and get hauled away. Near the tree we hand-dig to protect its roots.

Compact the ground first

The native soil under the base is compacted before any rock goes in, so the foundation itself can’t settle later.

Base in thin layers

Crushed rock goes in layer by layer, never dumped and tamped once. Each layer is compacted and checked for flatness before the next.

Grade for drainage

The surface slopes gently away from the house, so rain runs off and never sits against the foundation.

Level sand bed

A screeded bed of sand, left uncompacted, so every paver sits at exactly the right height.

Lay & cut tight

Your blend goes down in a relaxed pattern. Edges are saw-cut for clean fits, and locked in with edge restraint.

Compact, sweep, compact again

We compact the pavers into the bed, sweep in the joint sand, then compact again. That second pass is the one most crews skip.

Our rule

Compaction after the sand goes in

After the joint sand is swept over the finished pavers, we run the plate compactor across the whole patio again, with a protective pad so nothing gets scuffed. The vibration shakes the sand down into the hidden gaps and voids between and beneath the pavers, so the joints fill from the bottom up instead of just on the surface.

Then we sweep again to top the joints off, clean the surface and activate the sand. The result is tight, full joints with no hollow spots. Nothing shifts or sinks, and there are fewer places for weeds and ants to start.
